summary: Declare one canonical specification hierarchy and record every conflicting/superseding decision as an ADR with explicit supersedence links; run docs-as-code consistency review when any spec document changes.

evidence.summary: ADRs create a single durable source of truth per decision; decision log links to PRs/issues for traceability.
Microsoft Well-Architected guidance on maintaining an architecture decision record.
2026 SDD guide: versioned structured specifications as source of truth; community reports 60-80% fewer rework cycles vs prompt-driven development.

documentation-and-adrs (public, reputation established): read SKILL.md: 'ADR Lifecycle: PROPOSED -> ACCEPTED -> (SUPERSEDED or DEPRECATED)', 'Don't delete old ADRs ... when a decision changes, write a new ADR that references and supersedes the old one', plus 'Match the existing convention first' (inspect the repo's existing ADR location/numbering and surface the conflict rather than silently introducing a second scheme) and a 'Documentation for Agents' section naming which document owns what.

requires: docs stored in-repo and reviewed via PR
not_for: projects with a single spec document

risks: ADR discipline decays without review enforcement; stale ADRs can themselves mislead agents.
